newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate ends steady in flush market.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate ends steady in flush market.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate was unchanged at 6.00/10 percent as the market remained flush due to the inflow of overseas funds, dealers said on Tuesday.
They said many local and foreign banks were highly liquid, which had pressured all interbank rates downward.
The dealers said funds coming in from overseas on the back of a strengthening ringgit was more visible in the market.
The overnight rate dropped to 5.8/6.0 percent on Monday, from 7.5 percent on Friday.
One-week money was at 7.10/20 percent against 7.20/40, two-week at 7.20/30 against 7.30/40 and one-month at 7.20/25 against 7.30/35.
Three-month money was at 7.25/30 percent against 7.35 and six-month for 7.30/35 against 7.35/40.

Funds have been coming in from the spot foreign exchange market as well as swaps. The ringgit hit a 17-month high of 2.4690 a dollar on Monday morning on sustained buying by U.S. and Japanese funds, before retreating on profit-taking.
"Interbank rates seem to have just followed the overnight down. They should have been low last week too, but we don't know what happened," said the head of money dealing at a local bank.
He said there were rumours that Bank Negara was last week directly borrowing from select banks to prevent rates from falling. No confirmation was available from the central bank.
Bank Negara regularly intervenes in the market to keep liquidity under check or set interest rates. Sometimes it comes in to borrow directly from select banks, which are also its principal dealers.
